# NPM Improved v1.6.4 — Accurate node identification and clearer updates

## Node identification
- The control-plane health response now includes the configured NPMX node name and role alongside the independently detected physical Linux hostname.
- The header labels the physical server **Host** when the physical hostname is available; on older deployments it instead labels the NPMX configured node name **NPMX** rather than incorrectly representing a container hostname as a physical one or merely saying "Unidentified."
- Added the missing CORS-exposed response header for physical node identity when administrators use a cross-origin management UI.
- A fully provisioned native host updater writes the real host hostname into the project-matched readiness marker; new Compose installs already provide the read-only physical hostname mount. The old running Compose configuration is never replaced without the operator's approval.

## Update and maintenance
- When the installed release already matches the latest stable release, remove the redundant disabled "Update to [same version]" action and its unnecessary password prompt.
- Do not display rolling-cluster upgrade guidance when no upgrade is pending or in progress.
- Modern managed host-updater installations no longer show a permanent informational alert.
- A legacy updater now has a clear one-time repair action with a copyable host-specific command. This command downloads the matching public release's checksum manifest and updater tarball, verifies the SHA-256 checksum, then runs the native host installer on the Linux host. It never runs a helper container.
- Legacy host services cannot be automatically replaced by an unprivileged application container. A one-time host command is intentionally required on those existing deployments. Subsequently the native updater maintains itself on the host automatically.
- Preserves existing verified update handoff, rollback, NPMX version safety, 2FA, and session behavior.

## Verification
- Tests ensure cross-origin node identity header visibility.
- Tests cover generated host bootstrap commands, stable release validation and handling of project paths containing quotes.
